questions.q: In "Know housekeeping work Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Identify the provincial workplace safety body and find its page on cleaning and chemical hazards.
Use a timer and compare actual time with planned time for each room.
Lead others: train a helper using your standards and photos.
Explain the difference between cleaning, sanitising and disinfecting.

questions.q: In "Use tools and products safely Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Calculate the repeat-client rate: repeat clients divided by all clients.
Check each room with a checklist before you leave.
Name basic tools: cloths, mop, vacuum, scrub brush, bucket, gloves.
Describe daily, weekly and deep-clean tasks.

questions.q: In "Follow the rules in Canada Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Check each room with a checklist before you leave.
Compare surfaces: wood, stone, glass, steel, carpet; choose safe products.

Explain that hazardous products use standard labels and safety data sheets; read them before use.

questions.q: In "Clean to a standard Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Decline in clear words a task that is unsafe, such as cleaning from an unsteady high surface.
Name basic tools: cloths, mop, vacuum, scrub brush, bucket, gloves.

Build a room standard with photos of done and not done.

questions.q: In "Laundry, linen and special surfaces Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Identify high-touch spots such as door handles, switches, taps and remotes that need extra attention.
Lead others: train a helper using your standards and photos.

o: Identify high-touch spots such as door handles, switches, taps and remotes that need extra attention.

Explain why you must never post photos or details of a client's home.
